Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be a big <ACCENT_0001>tale
site containing <MATH_0003>. The underlying categories of the sites
<MATH_0004>, <MATH_0005>, <MATH_0006>, <MATH_0007>,
and <MATH_0008> have fibre products.
In each case the obvious functor into the category <MATH_0009> of
all schemes commutes with taking fibre products. The categories
<MATH_0010>, and <MATH_0011> both have a
final object, namely <MATH_0012>.

For <MATH_0001> it is true by construction, see
Sets, Lemma <REF_0001>.
Suppose we have <MATH_0002>, <MATH_0003>, <MATH_0004> morphisms
of schemes with <MATH_0005>.
The fibre product <MATH_0006> in <MATH_0007>
is a fibre product in <MATH_0008> and
is the fibre product of <MATH_0009> with <MATH_0010> over <MATH_0011> in
the category of all schemes over <MATH_0012>, and hence also a
fibre product in <MATH_0013>.
This proves the result for <MATH_0014>.
If <MATH_0015>, <MATH_0016> and <MATH_0017> are <ACCENT_0001>tale then so is
<MATH_0018> and hence we get the result for <MATH_0019>.
If <MATH_0020> are affine, so is <MATH_0021> and hence the
result for <MATH_0022> and <MATH_0023>.

<STRUCT_0001>
Next, we check that the big, resp.<SPACE_0001>small affine site defines the same
topos as the big, resp.<SPACE_0002>small site.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be a big <ACCENT_0001>tale
site containing <MATH_0003>.
The functor
<MATH_0004>
is special cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi from
<MATH_0005> to
<MATH_0006>.

The notion of a special cocontinuous functor is introduced in
Sites, Definition <REF_0001>.
Thus we have to verify assumptions (1) -- (5) of
Sites, Lemma <REF_0002>.
Denote the inclusion functor
<MATH_0001>.
Being cocontinuous just means that any <ACCENT_0001>tale covering of
<MATH_0002>, <MATH_0003> affine, can be refined by a standard <ACCENT_0002>tale covering of <MATH_0004>.
This is the content of
Lemma <REF_0003>.
Hence (1) holds. We see <MATH_0005> is continuous simply because a standard
<ACCENT_0003>tale covering is a <ACCENT_0004>tale covering. Hence (2) holds.
Parts (3) and (4) follow immediately from the fact that <MATH_0006> is
fully faithful. And finally condition (5) follows from the
fact that every scheme has an affine open covering.
